title: Council backs national urban park idea for Yorklands
subtitle: Heritage conservation district work for the Ontario Reformatory, staff's request to pause it, and the lack of public delegations.
overview: Council resumed its planning meeting after a long recess from November 13 and dealt with the draft Ontario Reformatory Heritage Conservation District Plan and Guidelines. The original motion to receive the report was withdrawn so a new motion could be heard first.

That motion supports, in principle, Urban Park Guelph and a House of Commons petition for a national urban park at the Yorklands site. It cites requests from the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation and support from the Six Nations of the Grand River. Council amended it to add "in principle" {{vote:m3}}, then adopted it as amended {{vote:m4}}. Council then received the staff report {{vote:m5}}.

For residents, the vote is an endorsement of a community-led proposal. It is not a commitment of city money or staff time, and it does not rule out other public uses of the site. Staff had suggested pausing the heritage district work while the park idea is considered. The minutes record no separate motion on a pause, and the transcript suggests that question was set aside until after this vote.

decisions.detail: Council added the words "in principle" so the city supports Urban Park Guelph and the premise of the petition on that basis {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Support for a national urban park
decisions.detail: Council recognized the requests of the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation and the support of the Six Nations of the Grand River, and supported in principle Urban Park Guelph and petition E-4593, notwithstanding other public uses or current staff direction {{vote:m4}}.
Council received Report 2024-487 on the draft Ontario Reformatory Heritage Conservation District Plan and Guidelines {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Staff said the federal and provincial governments are not subject to municipal heritage policies, so they preferred to pause the heritage district work while the park idea is considered. They noted a federal deadline of the end of 2025 to identify new parks.
Some councillors said the pause was only a staff recommendation that council could decline. One said many buildings and structures not yet protected could only be covered by the district plan.

Several councillors raised process concerns. The motion was not on an earlier agenda and no delegations were allowed on it. The chair and the mover replied that the community had already spoken through delegations, letters, a petition and lawn signs.

Councillors asked whether the motion would commit the city or limit other public uses. The mover said it makes no demands of staff, costs nothing and leaves other uses open. Staff said they understood it as not binding and not limiting the official plan.
A councillor asked whether the site was a realistic candidate. Staff said the idea is community-led and they had not studied it.
